import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { resetAndSeed } from '../support/seed';

// Line items can be changed or removed; the invoice total recomputes.
test.describe('edit line items', () => {
  test('removing a line item lowers the total', { tag: '@core' }, async ({ page }) => {
    await resetAndSeed({
      clients: [{ id: 1, name: 'Acme Ltd', email: 'ops@acme.example' }],
      projects: [{ id: 1, name: 'Website Rebuild', clientId: 1 }],
      invoices: [
        {
          id: 1, projectId: 1, status: 'DRAFT',
          lineItems: [
            { id: 1, description: 'Design', qty: 1, unitPrice: 100 },
            { id: 2, description: 'Hosting', qty: 1, unitPrice: 50 },
          ],
        },
      ],
    });
    await page.goto('/');
    await page.getByTestId('nav-projects').click();
    await page.getByTestId('project-open-1').click();
    await page.getByTestId('invoice-open-1').click();

    await expect(page.getByTestId('invoice-amount')).toHaveText('$150.00');
    await page.getByTestId('lineitem-remove-2').click();
    await expect(page.getByTestId(/^lineitem-row-/)).toHaveCount(1);
    await expect(page.getByTestId('invoice-amount')).toHaveText('$100.00');

    // That figure is derived from the rows on this page, so it drops whether or not the server
    // reworked what it stored. The project's invoice list reads the stored total — "update the
    // total when I do" is a statement about that one.
    await page.getByTestId('nav-projects').click();
    await page.getByTestId('project-open-1').click();
    await expect(page.getByTestId('invoice-row-1').getByTestId('invoice-amount')).toHaveText('$100.00');
  });
});

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start the Spring Boot app on $PORT (main class net.officefloor.hq.app.Application). On boot, Flyway
# migrates the empty in-memory H2 up to the current schema; Spring serves the SPA (static/) and the
# app's REST endpoints; the `e2e` profile enables the /__test__ seed endpoint. Returns once
# launching; poll /actuator/health for readiness.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
mkdir -p .run

: "${PORT:?PORT must be set}"
JAR="$(ls -t target/*.jar 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
[ -n "$JAR" ] || { echo "no jar in target/ — run bin/build first" >&2; exit 1; }

# Known audit file (the file-based test-assertion channel). Absolute so app + tests agree.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

nohup java -jar "$JAR" --server.port="$PORT" --spring.profiles.active=e2e > .run/app.log 2>&1 &
echo $! > .run/app.pid

content.text:
You can now change or remove charge lines on a draft invoice, and the stored invoice total is recalculated on the server each time. The acceptance test passes under `bin/e2e`. That test only covers removing a line, so I also tried an edit and a bad removal by calling the API directly against the running app. Changing a line to 2.5 × $40 stored the right total ($150.00), and removing a line that doesn't exist returned 404. I haven't clicked through the Edit/Save/Cancel buttons in the browser.

**Server** (Spring Boot — the app is Spring, not OfficeFloor, even though the package is named `net.officefloor`):
- **New endpoints:** `PUT /api/projects/{projectId}/invoices/{invoiceId}/line-items/{lineItemId}` changes a line, and `DELETE` on the same path removes it. Both return the updated invoice with its lines. A change uses the same checks as adding a line.
- **Rules:** both work only on draft invoices, the same as adding a line. On a sent or paid invoice they return 409, and an unknown line returns 404.
- **Total:** `Invoice` now recalculates its stored amount whenever a line is added, changed or removed. That stored amount is what the project's invoice list and the dashboard show. The changes are in `Invoice.java`, `InvoiceLineItem.java`, `InvoiceService.java` and `InvoiceController.java`.

**Front end** (`invoice-detail.ts`, `invoice.service.ts`):
- On a draft invoice, each line has **Edit** and **Remove** buttons (`lineitem-edit-{id}`, `lineitem-remove-{id}`).
- Edit switches the row into inline inputs with **Save** and **Cancel** (`lineitem-save-{id}`, `lineitem-cancel-{id}`). Enter saves and Escape cancels.
- After each action, keyboard focus moves to a sensible place, and errors appear in a `role="alert"` message (`lineitem-edit-error`). No existing `data-testid` was renamed or removed.

**Database:** I didn't add a migration because the existing tables already support this. Invoices can already be worth $0, so removing every line works.

Neither change nor removal writes an audit record; the spec doesn't ask for one.
